query: For the paper "Different Absorption from the Same Sharing: Sifted Multi-task Learning for Fake News Detection" (arXiv: 1909.01720), answer this question: What architecture does the rest of the multi-task learning setup use?

drafts:
The multi-task learning setup is built on a shared-private model, whose architecture is shown in Figure 2, and its shared-private feature extractor (and the attention sharing cell) adopts transformer encoder.

The paper proposes a sifted multi-task learning method "on the ground of shared-private model" to jointly train stance detection and fake news detection, filtering the outputs of the shared layer via a selected sharing layer; the model has a 4-level hierarchical structure shown in Figure 2, titled "The architecture of the sifted multi-task learning method based on shared-private model" [4][1]. The shared-private feature extractor and the attention sharing cell both "adopt transformer encoder" [3], and transformer encoder is used to acquire semantics from responses and forwarding of fake news [11].

Specif- ically, this cell utilizes input embeddings of the speciﬁc task to weight shared features for paying more attention to helpful features. The inputs of this cell include two matrixes: the input embed- dings of the speciﬁc task and the shared features of both tasks. The basic attention architecture of this cell, the same as shared-private feature extrac- tor, also adopts transformer encoder (the details in subsection 3.2).

3 Method We propose a novel sifted multi-task learning method on the ground of shared-private model to jointly train the tasks of stance detection and fake news detection, ﬁlter original outputs of shared layer by a selected sharing layer. Our model con- sists of a 4-level hierarchical structure, as shown in Figure 2. Next, we will describe each level of our proposed model in detail.
In this work, we utilize transformer encoder to acquire semantics from responses and forwarding of fake news for stance detection.
